While the bear cites a negative price-to-book ratio [E1], this anomaly highlights that the market is currently valuing the entity at a level that defies traditional accounting logic, creating a unique scenario where the equity is essentially ignored by broader capital flows [E2]. By focusing solely on the downward trajectory, the bear overlooks the extreme compression of the valuation multiples which already reflect the worst-case scenario [E1, E5, E6].

The bull’s argument that the market has already priced in the worst-case scenario is contradicted by the persistent, accelerating collapse in revenue, evidenced by compounded sales growth falling from -54% over ten years [E12] to -91% over the trailing twelve months [E15] and -98% year-over-year [E57]. Conceded: the P/E of -10.06x is numerically lower than the sector benchmark of 18.06x [E5], but this is a mathematical byproduct of persistent losses rather than a sign of conservative valuation. The bull’s claim that the market has discounted assets ignores the reality that the company’s ROA of -3.96% is significantly worse than the sector benchmark of 1.88% [E7], confirming that the remaining assets are failing to generate returns. Furthermore, the stock’s position at only 4% of its 52-week range [E4] demonstrates that market sentiment remains trapped at the bottom, showing no evidence of the stabilization the bull suggests. Relying on compressed multiples is a fallacy when the underlying business growth is decelerating [E58] and failing to keep pace with the sector median sales growth of 8.0% [E63].
